text: Name the capital city of a country in Asia.
flavor: Emperors carried their thrones from city to city. Name where the seat of power rests today.
rules: The capital of any country wholly or partly in Asia, so Russia, Turkey and Egypt count too, as do Taiwan and Palestine. Where a country has two capitals, either one counts.

answers.lore: Called Edo until 1868, when the emperor moved in from Kyoto.
Thais call it Krung Thep, short for one of the longest place names on Earth.
Built by the British as the capital of India, and inaugurated in 1931.
Russia's capital again since 1918, after two centuries of St Petersburg.
Chosen by Atatürk in 1923, over grand old Istanbul.
The coldest national capital on Earth.
Became the capital in 1997, when the government moved north from Almaty.
It counts because Egypt's Sinai lies in Asia, though Cairo itself sits firmly in Africa.
Called Frunze in Soviet times, after a Red Army commander born there.
Its name means 'Monday' in Tajik, after the market once held there on that day.
Holds the world record for the most buildings clad in white marble.
One of the few capitals with no traffic lights. Police direct the traffic by hand.
Unveiled as the capital in 2005. Its main road has up to 20 lanes and is often almost empty.
Malaysia's purpose-built seat of government since 1999, though Kuala Lumpur is still the official capital.
The seat of the Palestinian Authority, though Palestine names East Jerusalem as its capital.
Declared Yemen's temporary capital in 2015, after rebels seized Sanaa.
A purpose-built city east of Cairo. Egypt's ministries began moving in from 2023, and it took this name in 2025.
Greece counts for its eastern Aegean islands, which lie just off the Turkish coast.
Sri Lanka's official capital, where parliament has sat since 1982, though most people would say Colombo.

An Indian city, but not the capital.

Pakistan's second city, but not its capital.
Myanmar's capital until 2005, but not any more.
The last royal capital of Burma, but not the capital now.

Siam's capital for four centuries, until 1767.

A Philippine city, but not the capital.
An Indonesian city, but not the capital.
Indonesia's capital-to-be. Jakarta keeps the title until a decree says otherwise.
South Korea's temporary capital during the Korean War, but not now.
Home to many of South Korea's ministries, but Seoul is still the capital.
Capital of the Mongol Empire in the 13th century.
Kazakhstan's capital until 1997, but not any more.
A great Silk Road city, but not Uzbekistan's capital.

Islam's holiest city, but not Saudi Arabia's capital.
Syria's second city, but not its capital.
Capital of ancient Babylonia, in what is now Iraq.
The ceremonial capital of the ancient Persian Empire.

Afghanistan's first capital, in the 18th century, but not now.
An ancient city carved from rock in Jordan, but not its capital.

source: Copied from the daily question "capitals-asia" on 28 November 2026.
